response.name:
Response JSON containing the search query sent in the API call, and other response fields as follows: 
1. searchQuery: search query sent in the request 
2. page: page number of search results requested 
3. pageSize: requested number of results per page 
4. totalNumberOfHits: total number of results returned 
5. isExactTotalNumberOfHits 
    * `true` indicates that the search results in the JSON is the same no. of search results that logically      match the search query. 
    * `false` indicates that the search results in the JSON are lower bound because fetching all results is     too expensive to compute. 
6. groupingByDTOS: array of search results grouped on a field name 
7. groupIdentifier: field name that the search results have been grouped by 
8. groupBy: field value that the search results have been grouped by 
9. additionalInfo: shared information between groups, e.g. info if grouped by a security vulnerability 
10. searchResultItemDTOS: array of search results with each element containing an itemType, field names and values 
11. resultIndex: indicating the relevance of the search result w.r.t. the query

The response contains a list of vulnerability details corresponding to the vulnerabilitity or component identifiers.
  • `vulnIds` is a list of related vulnerability identifiers.
  • `vulnerabilityLink` is the link to the CVE or Sonatype Vulnerability Identifier description page.
  • `source` indicates the source from where the vulnerability details are obtained from.
  • `mainSeverity` is the official severity scores and vector strings assigned to the vulnerability.
  • `severityScores` are all other known severity scores not mentioned in the `mainSeverity`.
  • `weakness` indicates the source of the CWE, CWEId and the URI for the description of the CWE.
  • `categories` indicates the categories of the vulnerabilities.
  • `description` is the detailed description of the vulnerability.
  • `explanationMarkdown` is the text in markdown format for the explanation of the vulnerability.
  • `componentExplanationMarkdown` is the text in markdown format that is used to populate the vulnerability details in the UI.
  • `recommendationMarkdown` is the text in markdown format for a non-vulnerable component recommendationin the the UI.
  • `componentRecommendationMarkdown` is the text in markdown format for the recommended component.
  • `rootCauses`indicates the paths where the vulnerability is located, as well as the impacted version ranges of the vulnerable component.
  • `advisories`is a list of links to the published advisories.
  • `vulnerableVersionRanges` contains a list of the component version ranges that are vulnerable. Version ranges can be inclusive, denoted by square brackets [ ] or exclusive, denoted by ( )
  • `researchType` indicates if the vulnerability details were researched on FAST TRACK or DEEP DIVE basis
  • `isAdvancedVulnerabilityDetection` indicates if this vulnerability has been detected in entire files and embedded dependencies, typically beyond the pubic feeds, using our proprietary detection systems.
  • `customData` field contains the vulnerability attributes that are customized by the users, if found under the requested scope
  • `detectionType` indicates the type of vulnerability detection system used to obtain the vulnerability data. Possible values are PRIMARY, SECONDARY, AST, UNSHADER, OTHER or null.
    • PRIMARY means the vulnerability data has been investigated by the security researcher to explicitly implicate components referenced in the feed or is a result of independent research.
    • SECONDARY means the component has been implicated by our automated systems because it shares vulnerable code with components that were implicated by the PRIMARY systems.
    • AST means that the vulnerability is discovered as part of Application Security Testing and includes common issues such as code injection, authentication flaws and data leakage.
    • UNSHADER means the vulnerability is discovered by the Shaded Vulnerability Algorithm.

  • `recommendationMarkdown` is the text in markdown format for a non-vulnerable component recommendationin the the UI.
  • `componentRecommendationMarkdown` is the text in markdown format for the recommended component.
  • `rootCauses`indicates the paths where the vulnerability is located, as well as the impacted version ranges of the vulnerable component.
  • `advisories`is a list of links to the published advisories.
  • `vulnerableVersionRanges` contains a list of the component version ranges that are vulnerable. Version ranges can be inclusive, denoted by square brackets [ ] or exclusive, denoted by ( )
  • `researchType` indicates if the vulnerability details were researched on FAST TRACK or DEEP DIVE basis
  • `isAdvancedVulnerabilityDetection` indicates if this vulnerability has been detected in entire files and embedded dependencies, typically beyond the pubic feeds, using our proprietary detection systems.
  • `customData` field contains the vulnerability attributes that are customized by the users, if found under the requested scope
  • `detectionType` indicates the type of vulnerability detection system used to obtain the vulnerability data. Possible values are PRIMARY, SECONDARY, AST, UNSHADER, OTHER or null.
    • PRIMARY means the vulnerability data has been investigated by the security researcher to explicitly implicate components referenced in the feed or is a result of independent research.
    • SECONDARY means the component has been implicated by our automated systems because it shares vulnerable code with components that were implicated by the PRIMARY systems.
    • AST means that the vulnerability is discovered as part of Application Security Testing and includes common issues such as code injection, authentication flaws and data leakage.
    • UNSHADER means the vulnerability is discovered by the Shaded Vulnerability Algorithm.
